widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the stylized 3D brown bear defined by <Picture 1>: a very large rounded-square head, small round ears, short chocolate-brown fur, compact torso, short legs and rounded paws, beige muzzle, small dark-brown nose, thick expressive eyebrows, and large asymmetrical cream-colored eyes. Preserve this exact character identity. The orange background and floating question mark in <Picture 1> are not part of the character and must never appear.

<Video 1> is the source performance and environment. It defines the complete duration, framing, camera movement, nighttime street and bus-stop setting, body position, gesture timing, head and shoulder motion, mouth rhythm, lighting changes, and synchronized action timing. The original male performer is source motion only and must not remain visible.

<Audio 1> is copied completely from <Video 1> with its original timing, dialogue, ambience, and music.

summary:
Replace the original male performer in <Video 1> completely with <Subject 1>. The bear occupies the same screen position and follows the source performance timing while the surrounding street environment remains unchanged. Do not add a second character and do not preserve any part of the original man's face, body, hands, hair, or clothing.

detailed_description:
Create one continuous shot matching the exact length and camera behavior of <Video 1>. From the first frame to the last frame, only <Subject 1> appears inside the original performer's region. The bear reproduces the original pose sequence, pointing gestures, raised-hand emphasis, forward lean, head turns, shoulder rhythm, gaze direction, mouth timing, and final posture, adapted naturally to its compact bear anatomy.

Keep the bear's brown fur, beige muzzle, asymmetrical eyes, eyebrows, rounded paws, compact proportions, and facial identity stable in every frame. Integrate it into the cool blue-green nighttime lighting with coherent shadows and restrained motion blur. Preserve the source background, depth, exposure, framing, and timing.

No black silhouette, no black-filled character, no empty cutout, no remaining human, no human clothing, no hybrid anatomy, no duplicated subject, no orange reference background, no floating question mark, no character flicker, no identity drift, no changing fur color, no changing eye size, no duplicated paws, and no extra limbs. Remove all burned-in subtitles, captions, platform watermarks, account names, search labels, interface text and readable graphic overlays from every frame; reconstruct the underlying scene naturally with no text residue. Match the bear to the source plate in exposure, color temperature, shadow direction, contact shadow, depth of field, motion blur and atmospheric perspective. Preserve fine background detail outside the person mask. No hard cutout edge, no halo, no pasted-on appearance, no sudden black background, and no black or empty final frames. Keep the replacement complete and stable through the final frame.

overall_soundscape:
Copy <Audio 1> exactly and keep it synchronized to the original performance.

non_diegetic_music:
Retain only the music already present in <Audio 1>; add no new music.
nodes.title: 全帧低分辨率参考｜时间顺序完整 + SAM逐帧替换 + 原音频

widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the replacement character defined exclusively by <Picture 1>. Preserve the complete visual identity of <Subject 1>, including face, head shape, hairstyle or fur, ears, skin or material texture, body proportions, physique, clothing, footwear, attached accessories, colors, silhouette, and recognizable design features. <Picture 1> is the only authorized visual source for the principal character. If some body regions are not visible in <Picture 1>, infer them consistently from the same character design; never use any part of the original performer to complete them.

<Subject 2> is the principal performer appearing in <Video 1>. <Subject 2> is used exclusively as a motion, performance, spatial, and timing reference. Transfer the actions, poses, gestures, facial-performance timing, gaze direction, locomotion, body rhythm, object interactions, and scene positions of <Subject 2>, but preserve none of their visual identity, face, hair, body, skin, clothing, footwear, or accessories.

<Subject 3> represents all non-target content in <Video 1>, including the environment, architecture, furniture, vehicles, external handheld props, other characters, animals, lighting, weather, particles, shadows, reflections, and background activity. Preserve these elements unless they are physically occluded by the newly generated <Subject 1>.

<Video 1> is the complete temporal reference. It defines the shot sequence, duration, editing rhythm, camera movement, composition, focal-length behavior, framing, perspective, action timing, performance, scene continuity, lighting progression, and interaction structure. It must not define the visual identity of the principal performer.

<Audio 1> is the complete original audio track from <Video 1>, including dialogue, singing, breathing, vocal expression, environmental sound, sound effects, and music.

summary:
[reference generation + complete character replacement + motion retargeting + original audio reuse]

Regenerate the complete video using <Video 1> as the motion, performance, camera, timing, and scene reference, while replacing the entire principal performer <Subject 2> with <Subject 1> from <Picture 1>.

<Subject 1> must be the sole principal character from the first frame in which the performer is visible until the final visible frame, across every shot, cut, transition, occlusion, and change of scale.

This is a complete head-to-toe character replacement, not a face swap, head swap, costume overlay, texture transfer, partial replacement, or identity blend. No visible part of <Subject 2> may remain.

Preserve the original environment, camera language, action timing, object interactions, other characters, scene structure, and original audio. Remove all added subtitles, captions, watermarks, usernames, platform logos, interface elements, and promotional overlays.

retention_analysis:
- <Subject 1>: fully_preserved — preserve the replacement character’s complete and consistent visual identity.
- <Subject 2>: attribute_transfer_only — transfer only motion, acting, timing, pose, gaze, expression timing, and interaction data; preserve zero visual identity.
- <Subject 3>: fully_preserved — retain all non-target scene content, except removable subtitles, watermarks, logos, and interface overlays.
- <Video 1>: partially_preserved — preserve shots, editing, timing, camera, environment, lighting, actions, and spatial relationships; do not preserve the original performer’s appearance.
- <Audio 1>: fully_copy — reuse the complete original audio without rewriting, re-speaking, or generating new lyrics.

detailed_description:
Throughout the entire video, replace every visible occurrence of <Subject 2> with the complete <Subject 1>. The replacement must remain continuously active across all frames and shots, with no skipped interval and no temporary restoration of the source performer.

The replacement includes the entire visible character:

- face and facial features
- skull and head shape
- hair, fur, ears, horns, or head accessories
- neck and shoulders
- torso and waist
- arms, hands, and fingers
- hips, legs, feet, and footwear
- clothing and attached accessories
- front, side, back, and partial views
- cropped body parts at the frame edges
- motion-blurred body regions
- silhouettes, cast shadows, and reflections
- small or distant appearances
- defocused appearances
- partially occluded appearances
- character fragments visible behind objects

No source face, source head, source body, source limbs, source skin, source hair, source clothing, or source accessories may appear at any time. Do not combine the face of <Subject 1> with the body or clothing of <Subject 2>. Do not blend the identities of the two characters.

At the beginning of every new shot, <Subject 1> must already be fully established. Maintain the replacement when the performer enters or exits the frame, turns around, moves behind an object, crosses another person, becomes distant, passes through shadow, moves rapidly, becomes motion-blurred, or reappears after a cut or transition.

Transfer the complete performance of <Subject 2> to <Subject 1>, including walking, running, dancing, singing, speaking, turning, jumping, sitting, falling, hand gestures, finger motion, facial-performance timing, gaze direction, head movement, breathing rhythm, emotional intensity, and interaction with objects or other characters.

Retarget the motion naturally to the anatomy and proportions of <Subject 1>. Preserve the intended action, timing, center of mass, trajectory, contact points, and emotional rhythm without forcing <Subject 1> into the exact body shape of <Subject 2>. If the two characters have different anatomy or proportions, adapt joint motion, stride length, limb reach, hand placement, and balance so that the result remains physically plausible.

Preserve all external scene props from <Video 1>. When <Subject 2> holds, touches, rides, wears, pushes, pulls, or interacts with an external object, make <Subject 1> perform the same interaction with accurate contact, grip, weight, perspective, and occlusion. Attached clothing and character-specific accessories must follow <Subject 1>, while independent scene props must remain from <Video 1>.

If <Subject 2> speaks or sings, synchronize the mouth, jaw, cheeks, facial muscles, breathing, and emotional delivery of <Subject 1> precisely with <Audio 1>. Preserve natural phoneme timing without displaying lyrics or captions. When there is no vocal sound, avoid random or continuous mouth movement.

Match <Subject 1> naturally to the original scene’s camera perspective, scale, depth of field, focus changes, lighting direction, color temperature, exposure, shadow softness, reflections, motion blur, film grain, and image texture. Generate temporally coherent contact shadows and reflections for the replacement character.

Preserve the original camera movement, framing, focal behavior, shot duration, editing points, scene transitions, and background continuity. Do not add new cuts, zooms, camera movements, slow motion, speed ramps, freeze frames, or unrelated actions.

Remove all non-diegetic subtitles, captions, lyric text, watermarks, usernames, platform logos, interface elements, progress bars, borders, stickers, and promotional graphics. Reconstruct the covered background cleanly and maintain temporal consistency. Preserve text that physically belongs to the filmed environment unless explicitly instructed otherwise.

Strictly avoid: partial replacement, face-only replacement, head-only replacement, source body retention, source clothing retention, hybrid characters, identity blending, identity drift, missing replacement intervals, source-character reappearance, flicker, sudden appearance changes, inconsistent proportions, duplicated limbs, missing limbs, malformed hands, floating feet, sliding contacts, broken object interaction, incorrect occlusion, unstable shadows, unstable reflections, frame-edge remnants, and unfinished replacement during fast motion or shot transitions.

overall_soundscape:
Fully reuse <Audio 1>. Preserve the original dialogue, singing, vocal emotion, breathing, ambience, sound effects, spatial acoustics, and synchronization. Do not add spoken content, generated lyrics, narration, or subtitles.

non_diegetic_music:
Fully reuse the original non-diegetic music from <Audio 1>. Do not replace, remix, extend, or add music.
